segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: Imagine that you have a full-time job, but you want to take a year off to go back to school.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: What is it going to cost you?

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: Of course, there's the cost of tuition for your classes plus living expenses, but what about the money you're no longer earning at your job because you're now a student?

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: We call that the opportunity cost.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: Opportunity cost refers to the value of the next best alternative that must be given up when making a choice.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: It's a fundamental principle in economics that helps individuals and businesses understand the true cost of their decisions.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: My exercise in imagination illustrates a personal decision, but businesses also face opportunity costs in their operations.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: For instance, a company may choose to invest in new equipment rather than spend money to expand its product line.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: The opportunity cost of this decision is the potential revenue that could have been generated from the new products.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: Understanding opportunity cost helps individuals, as well as businesses, make informed decisions that maximize their benefits and minimize their losses.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: It's important to note that opportunity cost is not always measured in financial terms.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: It can also be related to factors like time, convenience, or personal satisfaction.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: For that reason, opportunity cost can be difficult to quantify, especially when dealing with non-monetary factors.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: Have you ever had to make a decision that included an opportunity cost?

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: Take a few minutes now to think, and then I'll ask for volunteers to share.
